scope:
Complete cleanup reviews through the shared Software report reader: full and compact Read review entries; captured architecture, 64-byte fingerprint, retained current/rollback identities, every obsolete generation ID, permanent deletion and retention rules, fresh-review requirement and explicit empty result. Three native mono short lines of at most 12 UTF8 bytes at 180x220 and 320x240; canonical full pages, page/arrow navigation, Back/Escape, full/compact/tiny resize anchors and preserved cleanup list position. Reader dispatch ignores deletion, reload, cleanup navigation, Stop/Cancel, application requests, typed and pasted commands. Pending partial/complete-before-exit review workers and approved writers refuse entry; existing literal fingerprint/argv, administrator approval and successful-exit admission are unchanged. Functional coverage includes 30/4096/empty generations, both architectures and maximum unsigned identities. Both existing cleanup allocation modes exercise decode, reader navigation/redraw/resize/ignored mutations, Back and owned cache retirement for 1000 cycles and retain zero tracked bytes. All 32 focused checks, independently staged maintained Software-only driver with all 25 allocation modes/fonts, ASan/UBSan functional plus standard cleanup mode and both full desktop architecture typechecks passed. Frozen compiler with nocache/fallback/reporting disabled; sanitizer leak detection disabled. No package service/protocol/authorization/deletion changes, whole-service/spawned-worker allocation freedom, guest graphical or broader publisher/catalog/runtime release qualification.
The optional maximum-size sanitizer allocation loop was deliberately stopped
after more than 21 minutes under heavy concurrent host load. It did not complete
and is not a passing check. The full sanitizer functional suite already covered
the 4,096-generation review, and its standard cleanup allocation mode completed
1,000 cycles with zero tracked bytes. The maximum-size allocation loop passed
without sanitizers both directly and through the maintained driver. No assertion
was relaxed. The original sanitizer logs, binary, generated C and interruption
note are pinned. Its parent only serializes results after every child finishes;
the three observed successful completions were recovered with seconds=-1 to
mark unavailable individual timings. No completed maximum-size sanitizer stress
result is claimed.
